svg.aria-label: A rights card summarising the position of anyone under eighteen in Uganda. She cannot lawfully be married, whether the union is formal or informal. She cannot in law consent to a sexual act, so an offence has been committed against her, not by her. Her agreement does not remove anyone's duty to protect her. She may return to school after childbirth under national guidelines. And she can call the Uganda Child Helpline on 116, free on any network, at any hour.
svg.text: If you are under 18 in Uganda
Five things that are true whatever anyone tells you.
You cannot lawfully be married.
Formal or informal, ceremony or none. Constitution, Article 31.
You cannot in law consent to a sexual act.
If it happened, an offence was committed against you — not by you.
Agreeing does not remove your protection.
Nobody’s duty to protect you depends on what you said or did.
You may return to school after a birth.
National guidelines say so. Being a mother does not end your education.
You can ask for help without your family knowing.
You do not need money, a phone plan or anyone’s permission to call.
Uganda Child Helpline
Free on any network
24 hours, every day
Ministry of Gender, Labour
and Social Development
Treasured Vessels Girls’ Centre, Jinja
General information, not legal advice.
